steps.message:
Before I touch it: `client.py` isn't staging-only. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points them at `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` on those two calls disables certificate verification for the production export too — that traffic becomes open to interception/MITM with no warning, and the change is invisible at the call site in `export_prod.py`.

So the "it's just staging" premise doesn't hold for this file as written. I'd rather not make the edit until you pick how to scope it.

options.label: Pin the staging CA bundle
options.description: Pass verify=<path to staging cert/CA> instead of False. Keeps real verification everywhere, but requires you to have the cert file on disk.

Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17`. Not committed.

Two things to be aware of:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` imports these same functions against `https://reports.example.com`, so that nightly finance export now runs without certificate verification.
- **urllib3 will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every call.** I left it unsuppressed rather than adding `urllib3.disable_warnings()` — it's the only remaining signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want it quieted.

No tests exist in the repo, and I didn't run the scripts (they'd hit live endpoints).
